notes: Existing single-region AWS credentials retain their original identity and region boundaries.
Additional regions are explicit, capped at four, and independently validated; partial inventory is never returned as success.
AWS Price List rates require pricing:GetProducts and cover Linux shared On-Demand compute only; EBS, IPv4, transfer, CPU credits and taxes are extra.
No production policies or saved account settings are changed by this source update.
Discovery has one None option per optional region, disables already selected regions and clears stale subnet choices before another preview.
Account preview reports bounded progress, preserves entries on failure, and keeps Save visible but disabled until validation and required network approval complete.
No additional cloud resources are created for this release verification; existing user scheduling remains authoritative.
OpenAI API review is not claimed without recorded response usage.

A forwarded installation declares DOB_PUBLIC_PANEL_PORT in root-owned service configuration. The public address is displayed separately; direct changes to its internal listener are rejected. Public gateway port editing requires an available gateway management adapter and is not implemented by this release.
Control recovery may run two expensive operations concurrently while weighted admission preserves provider and identity progress within the existing 24-connection pool.

Under DNS quota pressure, uncovered eligible servers precede additional endpoint allocation to already covered servers. Publication still requires current ownership, routing, transport and TLS evidence.

Readiness rejects disabled checksums, active recovery alarms and backup verification receipts older than 26 hours. Daily backup reuse requires the same sealed generation to be verified and less than 20 hours old; directory mtime cannot extend its lifetime.
Fresh installation uses an independently owned checksum-enabled cluster. Existing database identities remain authoritative; no automatic in-place checksum rewrite of unrelated or existing clusters.
TCP HTTP headers are optional and preserve existing routing, ownership, client policy and publication checks. They are incompatible with Reality and Vision.
VMess uses its JSON/base64 URI format. Shadowsocks uses the SIP002 plugin representation interpreted by v2rayNG; generic VLESS query parameters are not a universal Shadowsocks format.
Plain TCP adds no TLS. Existing compatible-client warnings remain for VLESS and Trojan on public IPs. Loopback native tests do not certify every Android client version.
Unavailable panels and provider authorization failures retain deletion intent and retry; neither a timeout nor an invalid cloud credential proves remote absence.
Migration 197 adds an index for completed inventory witnesses. It preserves all rows and the broader index used by other readers. The backlog regression deliberately runs before ANALYZE.

UDP capability enforcement is staged through DOB_UDP_CAPABILITY_PANELS (panel UUIDs, all or none). Native datagram evidence does not measure client/ISP latency or HTTP/3 throughput. The default scope is disabled for canary rollout.

Managed relays intentionally deny generic DNS/IP destinations. Their driver probes permitted-domain QUIC version negotiation only, without an HTTP request, and does not claim DNS capability. Migration 200 retains migration 199 history and binds evidence to the probe driver and donor plan.

DNS resilience is opt-in via DOB_DNS_RESILIENCE_PANELS. Empty/malformed/none retains the prior plan; disable for rollback. Explicit DoH performance profiles retain their own configured two HTTPS resolver endpoints.

Per-resolver TCP timeout is 2000ms with parallel queries and positive cache. If all upstreams fail on an uncached name, the pinned core may drop the query; the client controls its final timeout. This is not a two-second end-to-end DNS guarantee.

Client FinalMask capability does not mass-enable fragmentation on existing profiles. Shadowsocks SIP002 export remains explicitly unsupported by the v2rayNG importer; no Android device acceptance claim.
Country priorities are independent per account and opt-in; absent policy remains legacy AUTO. Existing routes, exclusions and security policies remain authoritative.

All ISO country choices are available, plus Kosovo XK. New creation and edits allow up to three distinct explicit countries. All AUTO preserves automatic selection; AUTO placeholders alongside explicit choices never authorize an arbitrary-country fallback.
Sticky drivers expose a finite six-session candidate budget. Unknown observations cannot authorize a lower country. This does not claim enumeration of every address in an unbounded provider pool.
Settings changes require the revision of the loaded draft. Reload an older cached editor before saving; a conflict preserves the current draft for review.
The attempted independent OpenAI API review ended with credit_balance_exhausted and no review output or usage receipt. It is not recorded as approval.

Provider browsing requires a verified sticky or fixed-egress proxy and the installed amd64 systemd sandbox. Missing isolation or country proof blocks launch. Each opening has separate cookies and storage, lasts at most 15 minutes and expires after two idle minutes. File uploads and downloads are unavailable.

Browser destination traffic uses the guarded proxy bridge. The application verifies country/IP and terminates the session on drift or failed proof; this is not a guarantee about unobservable provider behavior between observations.
evidence_location: Exact-commit source and installation results are attached through GitHub Actions. Production preservation evidence is recorded separately in private operations reports.
